name: Zagora Souk
hero_subtitle: A working regional market for dates, produce and everyday Draa Valley life.

overview.title: Dates, produce and local pace
overview.p1: Zagora’s souk is a working market, not a polished tourist bazaar. On market days the town fills with produce, dates, household goods and the rhythm of the wider Draa.
overview.p2: Come early for the best atmosphere. It is a place to watch and buy practical things more than to hunt for high-end crafts — Tamegroute remains stronger for pottery.
overview.p3: Keep valuables close and enjoy the ordinary energy of a southern oasis market.

food.p1: Sample local flavors around the market area and town centre.
food.li1: Fresh dates straight from the regional oases.
food.li2: Traditional tagines in nearby town restaurants.
food.li3: Local citrus and fresh seasonal fruits.
food.li4: Moroccan mint tea at local cafés overlooking the streets.
food.li5: Simple grilled meats and local bread.
food.p2: Carry small cash notes for small food stalls and vendors.

1.title: Market Days
1.desc: Wednesday and Sunday are the main bustling market days.

q1.question: Which days?
q1.answer: Often Wednesday and Sunday — confirm locally as patterns can shift.

q2.question: What to buy?
q2.answer: Dates, produce and everyday goods; pottery is better in Tamegroute.

q3.question: Crowded?
q3.answer: Yes on peak market mornings — that is part of the experience.

q4.question: Bargaining?
q4.answer: Normal for many goods; stay polite and clear.

q5.question: How long?
q5.answer: One to two hours is enough for most visitors.
